surprises.head: Anaheim found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Anaheim usually gets worse looks than most teams. Not tonight: a 10.7% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.0% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 350 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: Anaheim’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Anaheim’s power play has been near the bottom of the league for years. Not tonight: 16.7 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 7.1 and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

story.head: Carlsson sparks the Ducks back from two down
paras: A.J. Greer and Hunter McDonald fought midway through the first. Matvei Michkov and Porter Martone scored power-play goals just over a minute apart later in the period to put the Flyers up 2-0. It was a busy second period. Leo Carlsson and Greer scored four and a half minutes apart midway through the period to tie it 2-2. Tyson Foerster restored the Flyers’ lead shorthanded just under two minutes later, but Judd Caulfield tied it up for Anaheim a little over a minute later. Tristan Luneau put the Ducks ahead for good early in the third. Beckett Sennecke made it 5-3 on the power play later in the period, and that goal turned out to be the winner. Michkov scored his second of the night just over a minute later to pull the Flyers within one. Luneau finished with a goal and two assists.
The Flyers outshot the Ducks 32-26, but the Ducks’ chances were the more dangerous ones. Lukáš Dostál made 28 saves for the Ducks, and Joseph Woll stopped 21 of 26 at the other end.
Jackson LaCombe took three penalties on his own. The Ducks moved to 5-6-0, fifth in the Pacific, while the Flyers fell to 3-7-3, seventh in the Metropolitan.

items.text: The Flyers’ three-game winning streak is over.
The Ducks won for the first time in six games.
Leo Carlsson scored again against Philadelphia, and has five goals in seven games against them since 2023-24.
Matvei Michkov has a point in five straight games.
